clue.text: Typical of particular part of a log

definitions.meaning: first meaning: distinctive of a person or thing
second meaning: in mathematics, the whole-number part of a logarithm

explanation.surface: Something typical of one bit of a tree trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Log' suggests timber, but it is a logarithm: the integer part of a common logarithm has a technical name, distinct from the decimal mantissa.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a feature typical of something; the noun names the whole-number portion in logarithm tables.

clue.text: Letters conveying agreement

definitions.meaning: first meaning: mail exchanged between people
second meaning: a match or similarity between two things

explanation.surface: Letters that carry a message of agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both an exchange of written letters and a close match or harmony between two things.

clue.text: A game to cut short

explanation.surface: A match brought to an early end.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a book or speech is to shorten it by cutting material out.

clue.text: Strong declaration about rat noises

indicators.note: 'about' can mean around or astir, so the letters that follow are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone firmly states something about the sounds rodents make.
explanation.definitionFit: An assertion is a confident, forceful statement that something is true.

clue.text: They betray art revolution by one sort of change

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the word for creative work is read from its end

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round

indicators.note: 'sort of change' asks for the word sort with its letters changed about

explanation.surface: Turncoats who undermine an artistic revolution by changing sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Traitors are people who betray their country, friends or cause.

clue.text: Statement about the Left

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A press release concerning the political left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Left' sounds political, but it is the nautical left-hand side.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is an account or statement describing what happened.

clue.text: Alternative way with Scottish directions to make a furrow

indicators.note: an alternative way with something is a different arrangement of it, so the letters get reordered

parts.note: airts is a Scots word for points of the compass or directions

explanation.surface: Taking another route by following Scottish directions to plough a furrow.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is not in the clue as written: 'Scottish directions' must first become the dialect word AIRTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A stria is a narrow groove or ridge, as on rock or shell, a technical word for a fine furrow.

clue.text: Having no effect on sick person

definitions.meaning: first meaning (stressed on the second syllable): void, not legally binding
second meaning (stressed on the first syllable): someone disabled by illness

explanation.surface: A treatment that does nothing for a patient.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means void or without force; the noun, pronounced differently, means a person weakened by chronic illness.

clue.text: Battle with no rage involved is fruitful

definitions.note: adjective for a noun: the answer is a variety of fruit

indicators.note: involved means tangled or intricate, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A battle fought without fury turns out productive.
explanation.walkthrough: Despite the name, this is an English dessert apple, so 'fruitful' is a playful pointer rather than a strict synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The Blenheim Orange is an old English apple variety, so the answer is literally full of fruit.

clue.text: Most uncommon map, perhaps of interest to philatelist

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase rather than a noun

indicators.note: 'perhaps' hints the word is only a possible version, its letters loosely rearranged

explanation.surface: A very scarce old map that a collector might also want.
explanation.definitionFit: Philatelists collect postage stamps, and scarce issues are the ones they prize most.

clue.text: Bar returns from riotous feast

indicators.note: something that returns comes back the way it went, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a lever is a metal bar used for prising

explanation.surface: A pub's takings from a rowdy party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub, but it is a crowbar-like tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A revel is a lively, noisy celebration with drinking and dancing.

clue.text: Duck that is turning colour from the rear

indicators.note: turning round means the two-letter abbreviation just before it is written back to front

parts.note: i.e., abbreviation of id est, that is; read backwards

indicators.note: reading from the rear means the colour word is taken from its last letter to its first

explanation.surface: A duck whose plumage changes shade at the tail end.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider is a large sea duck, famous for the soft down used in quilts.

clue.text: Waterproofed cloth for common salt

definitions.meaning: first meaning: heavy tarred canvas sheeting
second meaning: an old word for an ordinary sailor

explanation.surface: A protective sheet for keeping table salt dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Common salt' looks like sodium chloride, but a salt is a seaman, and a common one is a deckhand.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarred canvas covers goods on deck, and sailors were once nicknamed after their tarred hats and coats.

clue.text: Prime mover before first performance

indicators.note: a mover shifts things about, so the letters of the preceding word are moved into a new order

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: The chief instigator appears ahead of the opening night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prime mover' reads as one phrase meaning originator; it splits into a word and its anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A premiere is the opening public showing of a play, film or other work.

clue.text: Manage to hear composer

indicators.note: to hear something is to take in its sound, so the spelling comes from what is said

parts.note: George Frideric Handel, composer of Messiah

explanation.surface: Contriving to listen to a composer's music.
explanation.definitionFit: To handle a situation is to deal with it or cope, a common synonym for manage.

clue.text: When saints disturbed model helper

parts.note: as in the sense of while or when

indicators.note: something disturbed is thrown out of order, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A holy figure, upset by unruly saints, becomes a model helper.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant is someone who aids or supports another person in their work.

clue.text: Type of shot leaving wounded hart in awful pain

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective qualifying the shot

indicators.note: 'in' places the first jumbled group inside the second
a wounded animal is knocked out of shape, so its letters are reordered

parts.note: letters to rearrange, then wrapped around the other group

indicators.note: awful suggests something messed up, so these letters are scrambled too

parts.note: a male deer; letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A hunter's parting shot leaves a stag injured and in agony.
explanation.definitionFit: Parthian horsemen fired arrows backwards while retreating, hence a Parthian shot is a sharp remark made on departure.

clue.text: Pedagogues with a book appear to be nodding

parts.note: New Testament, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: Teachers reading a book seem to be dozing off.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUT is the National Union of Teachers, a British teaching union.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutant is a botanical term for a flower or stem that droops or bows its head downward.

clue.text: Toy with cunning district leader

parts.note: a spinning top is a toy
arch as in roguish or sly

explanation.surface: A crafty local chief playing with a toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A toparch was the ruler of a small district or minor state in the ancient world.

clue.text: Go one better with music about pepper

parts.note: to cap a story or joke is to top it

indicators.note: 'about' means moved around, so the letters of the preceding word are reordered

explanation.surface: Outdoing someone with a song about seasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Capsicum is the botanical genus of sweet and chilli peppers, and the name used for bell peppers.

clue.text: Fop introducing company doctor to boatman

parts.note: the cox steers a rowing boat
Bachelor of Medicine, a medical degree

explanation.surface: A dandy introduces the firm's medic to a rower.
explanation.definitionFit: A coxcomb is a vain, conceited man overly concerned with his clothes, named from a jester's cap.

clue.text: William Bickerstaffe's kind of verse

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective describing verse

indicators.note: the possessive says the answer belongs to, and lies within, the name before it

parts.note: letters running across the two names

explanation.surface: A poet's favoured metre.
explanation.definitionFit: Iambic verse is built from feet of one unstressed syllable followed by a stressed one.

clue.text: Still standing around quiet city waiting for something

indicators.note: 'around' tells us one word surrounds the letters that follow

parts.note: the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: Someone lingering in a quiet town, hoping for something.
explanation.definitionFit: To be expectant is to be hopeful and anticipating that something will happen soon.

clue.text: Fabric first created by eccentric peer

indicators.note: 'first' asks for only the opening letter of the word that follows
something eccentric is off-centre and odd, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cloth invented by an odd aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: Crepe is a light fabric with a crinkled, wrinkled surface texture.

clue.text: Letter held back by teacher proves a big hit

indicators.note: something held is clasped inside the word that grips it

parts.note: pupils address a schoolmaster as sir

indicators.note: held back here means set the wrong way round, written right to left

parts.note: the letter X as it is spelled out

explanation.surface: A note kept by the teacher becomes a sensation.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a six is a shot clearing the boundary without bouncing, worth six runs; a sixer is that hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A sixer is a cricket stroke that sends the ball over the boundary on the full, the biggest scoring shot.

clue.text: Swear because hounds get early start

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter only

explanation.surface: Cursing because the hunt sets off at dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: To curse is to use bad language, the everyday sense of swearing.

clue.text: Show there's a party in progress on ship

parts.note: a do is a social event

explanation.surface: A celebration under way aboard a vessel puts on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on ship' means placed after the ship, so the vessel comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Brigadoon is a Lerner and Loewe stage musical about a Scottish village that appears once a century.

clue.text: Force leader's an outstanding painter

parts.note: chief as in principal or foremost

explanation.surface: The head of the police turns out to be a fine artist.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain each regional police force is headed by a chief constable.
explanation.definitionFit: A chief constable commands a British regional police force, its most senior officer.
